page: Microsoft Azure L8s_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine from the LSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The server is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 2002 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks place the L8s_v3 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1899.79 and a multi-core score of 7762.97. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 417.03 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 57.87 GB/sec and 37.8 GB/sec respectively. In database operations, the instance handles 8.0 million Redis SET operations per second. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the lower 25th percentile at 31.27 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L8s_v3 offers a high density of local NVMe storage and memory relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space without the overhead of larger compute instances. The hardware configuration is well-suited for database hosting, low-latency web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks, where the 135M parameter model achieves 193.77 tokens/sec for text generation.

Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers balanced performance across standard benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 5787.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 11432.18. Its memory subsystem provides 417.03 GB/sec of cached read bandwidth, supporting data-intensive operations. While multi-threaded bzip3 decompression represents a relative performance bottleneck, the server excels in database tasks, processing 8.0 million Redis SET operations per second. The L8s_v3 is qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-heavy workloads, making it highly suitable for database hosting, static web serving, and localized data processing.
